structure.summary: This document is a formal notice from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited to stock exchanges regarding the 26th Annual General Meeting (AGM) scheduled for June 24, 2025, via video conferencing. key_items: Sustainability and Inclusivity: Our Critical Pillars
Our vision aligns with India’s moment of logistics transformation
structure.summary: This text from APSEZ's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers the company's portfolio overview, strategic review, ESG overview, statutory reports, and financial statements. It highlights APSEZ's aggressive investments over five years, building a network of 15 Indian and 4 overseas ports with multi-cargo handling, hinterland connectivity, and integrated logistics. Digitalization efforts and an 18,000+ acre landbank support industrialization. Cargo volume CAGR of 24.1% (FY2002-25) versus India's 6.3% outpaced industry, meeting 5-year targets for cargo, revenue, EBITDA, and ROCE. The ambition includes generating over ₹1 lakh crore operating cashflow between FY2026-30, targeting 1 billion tonnes cargo by 2030 with international ports contributing 15% (up from 5%). Logistics is set for stellar growth with new trucking and freight forwarding segments; marine services expected to grow over 3x in two years. Financial foundation includes over 70% EBITDA-to-cashflow conversion and over 50% sticky cargo. Sustainability commitments: net-zero by 2040, 1,000 MW renewable energy (200 MW solar, 52 MW wind, 25 MW hybrid commissioned), 400 electric internal transfer vehicles, and global recognition (S&P Global CSA Top 10, CDP 'A-', Sustainalytics 'Low' ESG risk, ISS ESG 'Prime'). Community development, skill centres, employee safety, diversity, and strong governance with majority independent Board. The road ahead aligns with India's growth, Union Budget 2025 logistics-led focus. The CEO's message reports FY2024-25 performance: revenue, EBITDA, net profit up 16%, 20%, 37%; domestic ports revenue up 12% with 27% market share and 73% EBITDA margin; Mundra Port exceeded 200 MMT. Three growth pillars: Ports (acquisitions of Gopalpur, NQXT; operations at Vizhinjam and Colombo), Logistics (39% revenue increase, new trucking and freight forwarding), Marine Services (115 vessels after Astro Offshore acquisition). Net debt-to-EBITDA reduced to 1.9x from 2.3x. Vision to become world's leading transport utility through technology-driven infrastructure, aligning with India's century.

key_items: Unlocking lasting value by addressing key issues
structure.summary: The page covers APSEZ's materiality assessment, including how addressing key ESG issues unlocks lasting value by integrating materiality insights into strategic planning to align with stakeholder expectations, business performance, and environmental stewardship. It details APSEZ's approach to materiality: annual assessments since 2015 with biennial comprehensive reviews; the FY 2022-23 double materiality assessment; an FY 2023-24 internal review aligned with global ESG frameworks, sector trends, and peer benchmarking; and a current fiscal year bottom-up double materiality assessment following GRI Standards 2021 and ESRS, beginning with stakeholder identification per the AA1000 Stakeholder Engagement Standard.

structure.title: Structured Process to Materiality
structure.summary: The text outlines a structured materiality assessment process starting with organizational context understanding to identify ESG considerations. It details a four-step approach: Identify (using double materiality with impact and financial perspectives), Questionnaire Development & Stakeholder Consultation (engaging internal and external stakeholders), Assess & Prioritise (scoring and materiality matrix), and Monitoring & Validation (aligning KPIs with SDGs, integrating into ERM, annual review, CRO oversight, Board validation, and third-party assurance). The process considers sector dynamics, global benchmarks, and categorizes impacts as reversible/irreversible, short/long-term, and assesses likelihood and financial effects.

structure.title: Materiality Matrix

For Climate Change and Biodiversity, it details alignment with GRI standards, SDG linkages, KPIs, risks/opportunities, and mitigation measures, including carbon neutrality goals, renewable energy, biodiversity management plans, and mangrove afforestation. structure.title: Impact on external stakeholders
structure.summary: The text outlines two external stakeholder impact areas. Biodiversity and Land Use: caused by operations, affecting the environment and community; quantitative output metrics include changes in green cover and marine flora/fauna species; impact metrics cover mangrove and terrestrial plantation areas and monitoring of endangered species and biodiversity richness; negative impacts from ship movement, dredging, habitat fragmentation, deforestation, and coastal erosion threaten marine ecosystems and local livelihoods, requiring mitigation for sustainability and trust. Occupational Health and Safety: caused by operations, affecting social stakeholders (workers, suppliers, customers); quantitative output metrics include fatalities and ambient AQI near port/logistic sites; impact metrics cover safety training percentage, absenteeism rate, and mobile health clinic units; negative impacts include operational interruptions, employee absenteeism, reduced productivity, higher insurance premiums, and compensation costs affecting financial health.

structure.title: Managing risks and unlocking potential
structure.summary: The section details Adani Ports' Enterprise Risk Management framework, including a COSO-based approach, multilayered governance, the Risk Management Committee, the three lines of defence model, and the ERM process (Identify & Plan, Do, Check, Act). It covers risk culture through mandatory training and integration with business planning and incentives. The FY2024-25 risk exposure review lists top risks—political, regulatory, competition, financial, climate, industry, technology, project commissioning, community, geographic focus, land availability, human rights, debt repayment, returns, liquidity, and controls—each with descriptions, impacts, mitigations, opportunities, and capital at risk. It includes climate sensitivity analysis for port closures and interest rate/foreign currency impacts, and maps risks to capitals, material topics, strategic priorities, and ESG goals.

nodes.title: Our Approach to Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
nodes.summary: The text discusses managing risks and unlocking potential through a multilayered risk management system and robust governance framework aligned with the Group’s vision. It outlines the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) approach, based on the COSO framework, for identifying, prioritizing, managing, monitoring, and reporting financial and non-financial risks. Risk management is integrated with business planning and compliance. To promote risk culture, mandatory awareness and training programs are in place, including training for non-executive directors, function-specific training, and climate change/sustainability training. Risk criteria are incorporated in service development, and financial incentives include risk management metrics.

nodes.title: Risk Governance Mechanism
nodes.summary: The text details APSEZ's risk governance mechanism, integrating bottom-up and top-down risk management approaches. It describes the Risk Management Committee's composition and oversight, and the three lines of defence model with clear roles. It outlines the ERM process, including risk identification, analysis, evaluation, treatment, monitoring, and control, and mentions the ERM model (Identify & Plan, Do, Check, Act). It also covers management responsibilities, executive reporting, audit and assurance functions, board oversight, RMC meetings, risk management policy, and the risk assessment model using quantitative and qualitative data.

nodes.title: Risk Exposure Review and Top Risks with Mitigating Actions
key_items: Risk Exposure Review; Our Top Risks; R1; R2; R3; R4; R5; Key Risks and Mitigating Actions Capitals
Key Risks and Mitigating Actions Capitals
nodes.summary: The page presents Adani Ports' risk exposure review for FY2024-25, covering proactive risk identification, risk appetite approval by the Risk Management Committee, and quarterly assessments. It lists five top risks (R1–R5) spanning external political, regulatory, and competition risks, plus operational financial and climate risks, each with category, likelihood, impact magnitude, priority, and responsibility. It maps key risks and mitigating actions to capitals, material topics, management topics, strategic priorities, and ESG leadership goals. Detailed sections on R1 Political Risk and R2 Regulatory Risk include risk descriptions, capital at risk, impact on value, strategy at risk, material topics, mitigating measures, and associated opportunities.

nodes.title: Regulatory Risk
nodes.summary: This document from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers risk exposure review for FY 2024-25, including proactive risk identification, establishment of risk appetites approved by the Risk Management Committee, and quarterly assessments. It details top risks: political, regulatory, competition, financial, climate (physical & transition), and industry risks, each with category, likelihood, impact magnitude, priority, responsibility, capital at risk, risk description, impact on value, strategy at risk, material topics, mitigating measures, and associated opportunities. It also lists material topics across ESG, strategic priorities, and capitals (financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social & relationship, natural).

nodes.title: Adani Ports Enterprise Risk Management: Risks, Impacts, Mitigation, Opportunities
key_items: Risk Description; Mitigating Measure; Associated Opportunities; Associated Opportunities; Impact on Value
nodes.summary: The page covers enterprise risk management for Adani Ports, detailing risks R3 (Competition), R4 (Financial), and R5 (Climate). Each risk includes a description, impact on value, mitigating measures, and associated opportunities. Competition risk involves increased competitive ports reducing market share and pricing. Financial risk includes credit quality, liquidity, operational issues, and climate regulations affecting capital access. Climate risk covers physical and transition risks increasing operational costs. Mitigation measures include capital prudence, debt management, liquidity management, ESG disclosures, digital adoption, and end-to-end services. Opportunities include differentiation through investments and strategic growth headroom.

nodes.title: Industry Risk
key_items: Risk Description; Impact on Value; Associated Opportunities
Risk Description; Mitigating Measure; Impact on Value; Associated Opportunities; Mitigating Measure; Associated Opportunities
nodes.summary: The text covers three risk categories: Industry Risk, Technology Risk, and Timely Project Commissioning Risk. Each includes a risk description, impact on value, mitigating measures, associated opportunities, and strategy/material topics. Industry Risk addresses economic slowdowns, diversified ports, carbon neutrality, and strategic location benefits. Technology Risk covers cybersecurity breaches, investments in modernization, ISO 27001, and data analytics opportunities. Project Commissioning Risk discusses delays, project management expertise, and stakeholder engagement.

nodes.title: Geographic Focus Risk
key_items: Risk Description; Impact on Value; Mitigating Measure; Associated Opportunities
nodes.summary: The text addresses two risks: Geographic Focus Risk, covering its description (regulation changes, geopolitical tensions, supply chain constraints, weather patterns affecting port operations), impact (reduced competitiveness, operational slowdown, lower stakeholder confidence), mitigation measures (global presence, business mix improvement, data-based research for stable geographies, site-specific disaster management, climate vulnerability adaptation, asset productivity track record), and associated opportunities (relationship building, reputation enhancement, support for future projects, competitive edge, adaptability, resilience). It also covers Land Availability Risk, including description (land-intensive business, acquisition failure hindering operations), impact (reduced growth and competitiveness), and mitigation measure (centralized land management team).

nodes.title: Human Rights Risk
key_items: Risk Description; Impact on Value; Associated Opportunities; Mitigating Measure
nodes.summary: The text outlines human rights risk from value chain, workforce, and community exposure, with impacts on operations, credit/ESG ratings, and capital raising, plus mitigation via assessments, grievance mechanisms, and opportunities for reputation and productivity gains. It also covers debt repayment risk from long-term infrastructure financing, mitigated by ₹8,991 crore cash equivalents, and returns risk from cost overruns, revenue shortfalls, and rising costs, addressed through planning, timeline adherence, and cost optimization, with opportunities for lower-cost financing and improved creditworthiness.

nodes.title: Returns Risk
nodes.summary: The text outlines risks R11-R16 for Adani Ports: land availability, human rights, debt repayment, returns, liquidity, and controls. Each risk includes description, value impact, mitigating measures, strategy at risk, material topics, and opportunities. It also covers climate-related physical and transition risks, sensitivity analysis showing financial impacts of port closures (Mundra: ₹14 crore; all ports: ₹50 crore), climate vulnerability assessment for 12 ports under IPCC scenarios, adaptation plans for four at-risk ports, and sensitivity to interest rate and foreign currency risks.

nodes.title: Capital at Risk: Liquidity and Controls Risk with Climate Sensitivity
key_items: Risk Description; Impact on Value; Mitigating Measure; Associated Opportunities; Associated Opportunities; Integrating Climate Aspects; Sensitivity Analysis; Sensitivity to Financial Risks
nodes.summary: The page covers two capital-at-risk categories: Liquidity Risk (increasing capital requirements affecting balance sheet and liquidity) and Controls Risk (weaker internal controls causing errors or fraud). Each includes risk description, impact on value, mitigating measures, associated opportunities, strategy at risk, and material topics. It addresses integrating climate aspects, noting physical and transition risks, and presents sensitivity analysis showing financial impacts of port closures and climate scenarios at Mundra and other ports. It also includes sensitivity to financial risks from interest rate and foreign currency changes, with quantified impacts on profit after tax.

structure.title: Adani Ports Emerging Risks: Technological and Economic/Geopolitical
structure.summary: The page from Adani Ports' Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 discusses emerging risks that may become material in the medium to long term. It identifies two key strategic risks: technological changes and shifting geoeconomics. For technological risk, it describes workforce skill gaps in adopting automation, potential impacts on growth and competitiveness, and mitigating measures through smaller automation projects. For economic/geopolitical risk, it covers how changing interstate relations, protectionist policies, and geopolitical confrontations can shift cargo demand, detailing potential impacts on transhipment volumes and revenue, alongside mitigation through customer base diversification and ESG alignment.

structure.title: Pioneering the next era of infrastructure
structure.summary: The text outlines India's infrastructure growth opportunities driven by economic ambition, positioning APSEZ to capitalize on momentum through efficiency, innovation, and operational excellence, aiming to become the world's largest port operator and a leading Integrated Transport Utility with customer centricity and sustainability. It presents a strategic objective for sustainable global growth via assets, expertise, partnerships, and technology, followed by seven strategic priorities (ESG leadership, customer centricity, national and global expansion, business mix improvement, operational efficiency via safety/talent/technology/innovation, and growth through partnerships/acquisitions). It lists six capitals (financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social & relationship, natural) and nineteen material topics covering climate, biodiversity, water, waste, air quality, human rights, community, employee engagement, health & safety, customer satisfaction, DEI, labour relations, ethics, data privacy, risk, supply chain, regulatory compliance, geopolitical risks, and digital inequality.

structure.title: ESG Leadership
key_items: Way Forward; Way Forward; Capitals Deployed Risks
structure.summary: The text covers ESG leadership actions in FY 2024-25, including commissioning a 275 MW renewable energy plant and a 450 KLD effluent treatment plant, developing a 40-hectare grassland, and improving ESG ratings. It outlines future goals: carbon neutrality for ports by 2025, net zero by 2040, 1,000 MW renewable energy, zero effluent discharge, zero waste to landfill, biodiversity net positive impact by 2050, community skills training, safety and health programs, gender parity, and global governance standards. Performance metrics show 51% rail-to-road co-efficient improvement, 12% GHG emission intensity reduction, 4.5% women employees, 16% renewable power share, and 8,63,718 direct beneficiaries. Under customer centricity, it lists actions like an integrated trucking portal, conveyor system, immigration approval, digital gate passes, and indigenous tugs, with future plans for integrated solutions and ITUP leverage; performance metrics include 4.3/5 customer satisfaction and 19 new container services. For national footprint expansion, actions include acquiring Gopalpur Port, commissioning Vizhinjam transshipment port, concession agreement for Berth 13, O&M at Kolkata, container terminal at Gangavaram, increased market share to 27.0%, added warehousing capacity to 3.1 million sq. ft., and five new trains. Future plans include expanding port presence, scaling Vizhinjam to 3.2 MTEUs by 2028, targeting 1 billion MT global and 850 million MT India port handling, growing trucking to 200 MMTPA by FY 2029-30, starting ICD services at Malur and Virochannagar, expanding warehousing at Palwal, Kochi, and Kalyan, adding MMLPs in Hyderabad and Dadri to reach 20 by FY 2029-30, commissioning agri silos at 49 new locations to reach 94, and entering drydocking. Performance metrics show 27% market share in ports, 38 MMT capacity addition, 2,000 locations served, 13% container rail market share, 0.7 million sq. ft. warehousing addition, and 70%+ third-party marine services market share. Risks and material topics are referenced.

structure.title: Increasing Our Global Presence
key_items: Way Forward; Performing on Our Strategy
Way Forward; Performing on Our Strategy; Way Forward; Way Forward; Performing on Our Strategy; Risks
structure.summary: This text outlines Adani Ports and SEZ's FY 2024-25 strategic initiatives. It details global expansion through acquiring an 80% stake in Astro Offshore, extending maritime services to 9 countries, and securing a 30-year concession in Tanzania. It covers strategic priorities: improving business mix by entering new segments and increasing non-port revenue; scaling operational efficiency via technology, safety, and innovation; and growth through partnerships and acquisitions like NQXT. It includes performance metrics such as international volume and revenue, non-Mundra volume, revenue per employee, and container share. Future plans include expanding Colombo terminal capacity, extending marine services to 15+ countries by 2030, digital transformation, and integrating acquired assets for efficiency.

structure.title: Performance powered by financial strength
structure.summary: The text presents financial performance metrics across FY20-FY25: revenue from operations, PAT and PAT margin, RoCE, EBITDA and EBITDA margin (with exclusions noted for FY21 and FY22), net debt to EBITDA, net worth, net cash generated from operating activities, net debt and average maturity, and average debt cost, with values for each year and accompanying notes.

structure.title: APSEZ Operational Performance and Global Port Overview
structure.summary: The page covers APSEZ's operational performance and port network. It highlights 15 all-weather ports along India's coastline handling diverse cargo, balanced east-west coast capacity, and global expansion with operations in Haifa, Colombo West International Terminal, and approved acquisition of North Queensland Export Terminal. It includes a map showing port locations, capacities (total ~361 MMT, west ~272 MMT, east ~15633 MMT), and connectivity to dedicated freight corridors, feeder routes, and port types (multipurpose, container, bulk).

structure.title: Mundra Port
structure.summary: The text covers Mundra Port, APSEZ's flagship port in Gujarat, detailing its strategic location, infrastructure including 27 berths and 2 single point moorings, and its capability to handle diverse cargo like dry bulk, containers, and crude oil. Key statistics include 264 MMT installed capacity and 200.7 MMT cargo volume handled. Highlights cover operational records in cargo, container, vessel, and railway movements, and infrastructure improvements like weighbridge relocation reducing congestion. Awards and accolades include Shipping Terminal of the Year, Blue Planet Award, and recognition in the World Bank's Container Ports Performance Index, plus a special postal stamp for its silver jubilee.

structure.title: Adani Ports Tuna and Dahej Terminals Overview
structure.summary: This page from Adani Ports' 2024-25 Annual Report details two terminals. Tuna Terminal, an all-weather port in Gujarat, handles dry and break-bulk cargo with mechanized facilities, warehouses, and rail/road connectivity. Highlights include new commodities, mobile hopper, weighbridges, solar LED lights, enhanced dust suppression, record cargo volumes (1.07 MMT monthly, 47,910 MT daily), and a Gold Award in Waste Management. Key statistics: 14 MMT capacity, 9.4 MMT handled. Dahej Port, a deep-water multi-cargo port, features mechanized handling, Panamax accommodation, and India's first elevated coal conveyor. Highlights include AI-based gantry protection, fibre optic communication, IVMS/ADAS, solar streetlights, automated dashboards, and an International Safety Award. Key statistics: 16 MMT capacity, 10.3 MMT handled.

structure.title: Port Operations and Highlights: Hazira, Dighi, and Mormugao
structure.summary: This page from Adani Ports and SEZ's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 profiles three port assets. Hazira Port is described as a key multi-cargo hub in Gujarat with capacity, connectivity, and operational highlights including new cargo categories, reduced delays, and digital initiatives. Dighi Port is positioned as a Maharashtra gateway with storage and handling capabilities, noting its maiden steel plates cargo and certifications. Mormugao Terminal is a coal/coke handling facility under a DBFOT agreement, highlighting operational and environmental upgrades. Each section includes key statistics on installed capacity and cargo volumes handled.

structure.title: Vizhinjam Port
structure.summary: This case study on Vizhinjam Port, India's first mega transshipment container terminal and automated port, covers its strategic location, deep draft, and phase-I operations starting December 3, 2024, with infrastructure details. It highlights commercial operations, including handling the largest container vessel in India, and key statistics like installed capacity and cargo volumes. The text details the indigenously developed Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) with its features and benefits. It also covers automation innovations such as remote-operated quay cranes, automated yard cranes, OCR-powered quayside processes, AI-powered gate systems, and RTLS-equipped ITVs. Awards and accolades, including the British Safety Council Award, are mentioned. The document also includes portfolio, corporate, ESG, and financial overview sections as part of the integrated annual report.

structure.title: Karaikal, Kattupalli Ports and Ennore Terminal Overview
structure.summary: The page profiles Karaikal Port (an all-weather deep-sea port in Puducherry handling dry-bulk, break-bulk, and liquid cargo with mechanised facilities and multimodal rail links), highlighting first-time cargo handling, a consolidated PMT contract, equipment upgrades, record vessel and despatch milestones, and horticulture water reuse, with key statistics on capacity and volumes. It then covers Kattupalli Port (multi-cargo facility with three berths, DPD, on-dock CFS, and Panamax capability) and Adani Ennore Container Terminal (a JV with Terminal Investment Ltd offering 24/7 access and rail links), summarizing operational efficiency gains, record cargo volumes, the GEMINI service launch, renewable energy use, water savings, and environmental awards, plus capacity and volume statistics.

structure.title: Krishnapatnam and Gangavaram Ports: Overviews, Highlights, and Key Statistics
structure.summary: The page covers Krishnapatnam Port and Gangavaram Port, each with an overview, highlights, and key statistics. Krishnapatnam Port in Andhra Pradesh features a 3,250m wharf, 14 vessels berthing, deep draft for Super Capesize, five cape-enabled berths, multimodal connectivity, and operational efficiency. Highlights include electrified cranes, vehicle management system, LPG vessel, vessel records, awards, and statistics (75 MMT capacity, 55 MMT cargo). Gangavaram Port, an all-weather deep-water port with 9 berths up to 19.5m, mechanised systems, new container terminal, and connectivity, serves eight states. Highlights include container terminal launch, cranes, scanner, records, saplings, awards, and statistics (64 MMT capacity, 27 MMT cargo).

structure.title: Dhamra and Gopalpur Ports: Overview, Highlights, and Key Statistics
structure.summary: The page covers two ports under Adani Ports and SEZ Limited. Dhamra Port is described as an all-weather, deep-draft port in Odisha with five berths, rail connectivity, rapid loading silos, and multi-cargo handling. Its highlights include crane productivity improvements, cargo movement initiatives, cyclone resilience, record monthly cargo and rakes, renewable energy use, water conservation, and awards. Key statistics show 50 MMT installed capacity and 46 MMT cargo handled. Gopalpur Port is an all-weather, deep-draft port on India's east coast with 800m berth length, 14.5m draft, 2.5 km entrance channel, storage facilities, and connectivity to Odisha, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh. Highlights include SAP and iPortman implementation, new commodities, and EOL rake operations. Key statistics show 20 MMT installed capacity and 2.6 MMT cargo handled.

structure.title: APSEZ Port Operations: Kolkata, Haldia, and Haifa
structure.summary: The page covers APSEZ's port operations. Kolkata Port: a 5-year contract for container handling equipment at Kolkata Dock System, operations started December 2024, equipped with MHCs and RTG cranes, plans for additional equipment, and synergies with transshipment hubs. Haldia Terminal (under construction): a dry bulk terminal with ~4 MMTPA capacity, 30-year concession, mechanized with rail and road evacuation, and specifications. Haifa Port: APSEZ holds 70% stake in consortium that acquired Haifa Port, Israel's largest, handling diverse cargo, connected to railway, part of IMEC corridor. Highlights: operational continuity in war zone, new equipment, renewed agreements, new container line agreements, cement handling agreement, livestock handling, and air quality monitoring collaboration. Key statistics: 26 MMT installed capacity, 10.6 MMT cargo volumes handled.

structure.title: Colombo West International Terminal
structure.summary: APSEZ acquired Container Terminal 2 (CT2) in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania's largest container facility, serving 79% of port container movement and acting as a gateway to East Africa. Highlights include Navis N4 TOS and billing system deployment, Fixed Berthing Window introduction, reduced vessel waiting time from 22 to under 5 days, employee exchange program, and online safety incident reporting with sensor upgrades. Key statistics: 15 MMT capacity, 9 MMT cargo handled in FY 2024-25. The Colombo West International Terminal (CWIT) is being developed as a 35-year BOT with John Keells Holdings and Sri Lanka Ports Authority, featuring 3.2 Mn TEU capacity, 24 MMT Phase 1 capacity, 20m quay depth, and ability to handle three 24,000 TEU vessels simultaneously with a 100% electric fleet of 62 ITVs; network impact includes 10 terminals across 15 Indian ports handling over 11 Mn TEUs annually. APSEZ Logistics offers end-to-end services with 12 MMLPs, 132 rakes, 900+ trucks, 3.1 million sq.ft. warehousing, and 1.2 MMT agri-silos. Key logistics statistics: 12 MMLPs, 132 rakes, 937 trucks, 3.1 million sq.ft. warehousing, 68 container rakes handling 6,43,479 TEUs, 54 bulk rakes, 7 agri rakes, 111 routes (44 EXIM, 67 domestic), 21.97 MMT goods transported, 34 locations across 18 states, 1,93,573.5 kL liquid cargo at Kanech Terminal, and 3 AFTO rakes transporting 16,647 cars.

It presents key statistics: 12 multi-modal logistic parks, 132 rakes, 937 trucks, 3.1 million sq. ft. warehousing space, and 1.2 MMT agri-silos. Highlights detail the rake fleet: 68 container rakes handling 6,43,479 TEUs, 54 bulk rakes under GPWIS, and 7 agri rakes, operating on 111 routes (44 EXIM, 67 domestic). Cargo handled across India totals 21.97 MMT (coal, limestone, iron ore).

It details 3 AFTO rakes owning/operating 16,647 cars transported, and major terminals (Patli, Virochannagar, Nagpur, Tumb, Kishangarh) with EXIM/domestic services, handling capacities, demand centers, DFC advantages, and facilities like auto/steel yards, cold storage, and Grade-A warehouses. It covers Trucking Management Solutions integrating trucks for first/last-mile with real-time tracking and optimized routing, Warehousing with 3.1+ million sq ft capacity and 937 trucks, and Agri Logistics with 90 storage facilities (20 operational, 70 under construction) in 9 states, 7 agri rakes, 4.0 MMT silo capacity, and plans to increase market share to 63% with over 4 MMT capacity by FY 2025-26.

structure.title: Integrated Logistics Terminals, Warehousing, TMS, and Agri Logistics Overview
structure.summary: The page provides an integrated annual report overview of Adani Ports and SEZ logistics infrastructure for 2024-25. It details major inland terminals at Patli, Virochannagar, Nagpur, Tumb, and Kishangarh, covering EXIM/domestic services, annual TEU handling capacities, key demand centers, DFC corridor advantages, double stacking, and facilities like auto/steel yards, cold storage, and Grade-A e-commerce warehouses. It describes Trucking Management Solutions (TMS) offering first and last-mile fleet services with real-time tracking and demand-based pricing, warehousing with 3.1+ million sq. ft. capacity and 937 trucks, and Agri Logistics featuring India’s first integrated bulk grain handling system, 90 storage facilities, 7 agri rakes, and 4.0 MMT silo capacity, with plans to reach 63% market share by FY 2025-26.

structure.title: Adani Ports Marine Services and Tugs Overview
structure.summary: The page covers Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Marine Services division, including tugs and operational performance. It details tug operations serving captive and third-party deployments under long-term take-or-pay contracts, with a young fleet focused on modernisation, agility, and revenue optimisation. The marine division comprises Ocean Sparkle Ltd., Astro Offshore, and The Adani Harbour International DMCC, operating 115 third-party vessels across major Indian ports and strategic locations, with Astro Offshore extending global reach. Adani Harbour Services Ltd. operates 46 vessels across APSEZ ports, and APSEZ leads capital dredging with 28 dredgers.

structure.title: Offshore Support Vessels and Dredgers Fleet Overview
structure.summary: The page covers APSEZ's offshore support vessels and dredgers. It details the acquisition of Astro Offshore, adding 26 OSVs (AHTs, barges, MPSVs, workboats) with an average age of 11 years, strengthening presence in the Middle East, Far East Asia, and Africa, and adding Tier-1 clients in EPC, oil & gas, and renewables. Highlights include deploying indigenously built ASTDS tugs, placing India's largest order for eight tugs with Cochin Shipyard, and commencing operations with India's first foreign-flagged tugboat at Mundra. For dredgers, APSEZ operates 28 dredgers, making it India's largest dredging operator and largest private player in capital dredging, offering capital, maintenance, and inland dredging services, including for National Waterway NW-1.

structure.title: Environment
structure.summary: The text from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers their environmental initiatives, particularly climate change. It details their goal to be Carbon Neutral by 2025 and Net-Zero by 2040, outlining their climate strategy focused on reducing emissions, using renewable energy, and improving energy efficiency. It discusses a Climate Vulnerability Risk Assessment identifying vulnerable ports (Mundra, Dhamra, Hazira, Krishnapatnam) and the risks from sea-level rise. It presents their approach to reduce impact, build resilience, and strengthen systems, along with five levers of their Net-Zero journey. The text also describes climate governance structure, including the Board and committees, ESG team, and risk management processes. It highlights climate action alignment with global agreements like the Paris Agreement and COP 29, commitments to SBTi, and progress towards carbon neutrality, such as deployment of electric vehicles and renewable power usage.

structure.summary: The text outlines APSEZ's climate strategy in its 2024-25 Integrated Annual Report, aiming for carbon neutrality by 2025 and net-zero by 2040. It details five levers: sustainable infrastructure, process optimization, standards compliance, resource planning, and legal compliance. It covers climate vulnerability assessments identifying Mundra, Dhamra, Hazira, and Krishnapatnam ports as at-risk, and mentions a climate governance framework led by the Board with committees. structure.title: ` 137 crore
structure.summary: The section details a 137 crore breakwater construction expenditure and seven Kyoto Protocol greenhouse gases. It covers APSEZ's focus on reducing Scope 2 emissions via renewable energy and Scope 1 emissions through electrification and efficiency, reporting 32% Scope 1 share, emissions below FY 2024-25 targets, and decreased emission intensity despite increased absolute emissions. It presents emission intensity and absolute emission trends from FY16 to FY25, ozone-depleting substance quantities, Scope 3 emissions inventory by category with methodology comparing FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24, and energy performance: ISO 50001 certification, energy management strategies, total energy consumption (3,790 TJ, up 10%), declining energy intensity (117 GJ/crore from 122), renewable share (16%), 100% renewable electricity target by 2025, business-unit energy consumption, LED lighting upgrades, and noise management including impact identification, reduction, monitoring, equipment standards, and marine ecosystem impacts.

nodes.title: Focus on Reducing Scope 2 Emissions
nodes.summary: The text covers a 137 crore breakwater construction expenditure and lists seven Kyoto Protocol greenhouse gases. It details APSEZ's focus on reducing Scope 2 emissions through renewable energy integration and Scope 1 emissions via electrification and energy efficiency. It reports 32% Scope 1 share, emissions below FY 2024-25 targets, and decreased emission intensity despite increased absolute emissions. It includes emission intensity and absolute emission trends from FY16 to FY25, ozone-depleting substance quantities, and a Scope 3 emissions inventory by category with methodology, comparing FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24 totals.

nodes.title: Adani Ports FY2024-25 Emissions Performance and Targets
key_items: We have successfully achieved emissions levels well below our targeted amounts for the fiscal year 2024-25.
nodes.summary: This page from Adani Ports' Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers emissions performance. It notes Scope 1 emissions are 32% of total Scope 1+2, mainly from fossil fuels in owned equipment. The company achieved emissions below FY2024-25 targets. It provides target figures for Scope 1, 2, and 3, and states emissions intensity for Scope 1 and 2 was significantly lower than the previous year. Absolute emissions rose with business growth, but emission intensity per revenue slightly decreased. Strategies to reduce Scope 1 include alternative fuels, electrification, and energy efficiency. Charts show emission intensity and emissions from FY16 to FY25. A table lists ozone-depleting substances quantities.

nodes.title: Scope 3 - Inventory Group (Category-Wise)
nodes.summary: The text covers APSEZ's Scope 3 emissions inventory, detailing all 15 GHG Protocol categories plus other upstream/downstream sources, with FY2024-25 and FY2023-24 emissions data in tCO2e and total upstream, downstream, and overall totals. It also addresses energy performance: ISO 50001 certification at ports and JVs, energy management strategies including monitoring, audits, targets, renewable energy adoption, electrification, and alternative fuels. It reports total energy consumption (3,790 TJ in FY2024-25, up 10% due to new ports) and declining energy intensity (117 GJ/crore from 122), with breakdowns of fuel and electricity consumption, renewable energy share (16%), and a target of 100% renewable electricity by 2025.

nodes.title: APSEZ Energy Performance and Management Strategy FY 2024-25
nodes.summary: The page covers APSEZ's energy performance, including its ISO 50001:2018 certified Energy Management System, strategies for energy efficiency, renewable energy adoption, and monitoring. It details total energy consumption (3,790 TJ, up 10% due to new ports) and energy intensity decline (122 to 117 GJ/crore), with graphical data on fuel vs. electric energy trends from FY20 to FY25. It breaks down material-wise energy consumption (e.g., fuel types like FO/HFO, diesel) and total electricity consumption, showing renewable share (16% in FY25 vs. targets). The strategy focuses on awareness, electrification, alternative fuels, and new technologies, with regular audits and KPIs, aiming for 100% renewable electricity by 2025.

nodes.title: APSEZ Energy Efficiency and Noise Management Overview
nodes.summary: The page presents Adani Ports and SEZ's FY2024-25 data on business-unit energy consumption across ports, logistics, hospitals, dredging, agri-logistics, and harbour services, broken down into total, grid, fuel, and renewable energy, plus energy intensity trends from FY16 to FY25. It details energy-reduction measures such as LED lighting upgrades. It also addresses noise management, noting it is not a primary material concern but covering impact identification, reduction, ambient monitoring, regulatory reporting, equipment standards below 75 dB(A), maintenance, greenbelts, acoustic enclosures, and PPE. It examines noise impacts on marine ecosystems through mapping and initiatives like closed ship engine doors, insulation, and maintenance, along with scheduling high-noise activities and compliance reporting.

structure.title: Water stewardship
key_items: Business Unit-Wise Water Consumption; Water Consumption Details; Water Consumption & Water Withdrawal (ML)
structure.summary: This text from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers water stewardship. It discusses the global water crisis, including scarcity, pollution, and climate impacts, and the need for businesses to manage water risks. It outlines APSEZ's commitment to responsible water management, including its Water Stewardship Policy, alignment with the CEO Water Mandate, and collaboration with stakeholders. Key measures include adoption of sustainable practices, water-efficient technologies, and regular monitoring. The text details water targets for 2025: 60% reduction in water consumption intensity, 83% withdrawal from non-competing sources, and less than 20% freshwater withdrawal share. It also presents the water management approach with seven points, water performance data, business unit-wise water consumption, key metrics for FY 2024-25 (7% increase in net fresh water consumption, 62% reduction in water intensity, 97% consumption by ports, 1,129 ML recycled), and water consumption details from FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25. The report emphasizes continuous improvement, transparency, and community engagement in water management.

structure.title: Wastewater management
structure.summary: This text from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers their wastewater management strategy, including principles of reduction, recycling, and reuse. It details water withdrawal sources by percentage, wastewater management initiatives like zero liquid discharge and 98% recycling, and the wastewater management hierarchy. It outlines water conservation initiatives such as audits, monitoring, and rainwater harvesting. A case study describes the commissioning of a 450 KLD effluent treatment plant at Adani Hazira Port, including its objective, project description, activities, methodology, cost (₹25.24 crore), and benefits like biogas utilization and recycling of 300 KLD.

structure.title: Waste management
structure.summary: The section on waste management covers APSEZ's strategy for resource conservation through material management, waste reduction, recycling, reuse, and co-processing to achieve cost savings, environmental footprint reduction, productivity enhancement, and employee pride. It details compliance with regulations for ship-originated and port-related waste, including hazardous, bio-medical, e-waste, and construction debris, with disposal at authorized facilities. The Zero Waste to Landfill initiative aims to divert all waste from landfills using the 5R approach, with measures like composting, recycling, co-processing, and employee training. Waste KPIs track quantities generated, processed, and disposed, reporting zero waste to landfill at 12 sites and a 32% waste intensity reduction. Waste by category across FY22-25 is detailed, along with an Integrated Waste Management System based on 5Rs, single-use plastic elimination, and outcomes such as recycling, biogas generation, and zero waste to landfill at 12 ports.

nodes.title: We are Committed to Resource Conservation Through
nodes.summary: The text covers the company's waste management strategy, emphasizing effective material management and waste reduction to achieve cost savings, environmental footprint reduction, productivity enhancement, and employee pride. It outlines measures like sustainable consumption, resource reduction, minimizing toxic materials, and limiting waste and marine pollutants. It details commitments to resource conservation through recycling, reuse, and co-processing to reduce landfill waste. It addresses marine waste management across port life cycles, including dredged materials, ship-generated garbage, and cargo waste. It highlights strict compliance with regulations for ship-originated and port-related waste, including hazardous, bio-medical, e-waste, and construction debris. Disposal procedures at APSEZ are described, with hazardous and bio-medical waste handled at authorized facilities, and e-waste and batteries sent to authorized recyclers per 2016 rules. Successful implementation of waste reduction and proper disposal via authorized TSDF is noted, along with compliance with resource recovery principles.

nodes.title: APSEZ Waste Management, Recycling and Zero Waste to Landfill Overview
nodes.summary: This page from Adani Ports and SEZ's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers waste management under three sections: Recycling & Reuse, Zero Waste to Landfill, and 5Rs of Waste Management (%). It describes environmental programmes prioritizing source recycling, collaboration within the SEZ, and joint solutions to minimize waste impacts. The Zero Waste to Landfill initiative aims to divert all waste from landfills via responsible non-hazardous waste disposal and the 5R approach across facilities. Key FY 2024-25 measures include composting biodegradable waste, recycling paper, plastic and scrap, co-processing dry waste in cement plants, using STP sludge as manure, and employee training. Waste KPIs track quantities generated, processed via 5R, and disposed. The page reports zero waste to landfill achieved at 12 sites, with 38% recycled, 4% reused, 18% reprocessed, 15% recovered, and specific hazardous, e-waste, biomedical, horticulture, battery and metal scrap figures. It notes a 30% waste intensity reduction target by 2025 versus FY 2017-18, achieved at 32%, elimination of single-use plastics, and sale of 6,196 MT metal scrap.

nodes.title: APSEZ Waste Management: Practices, Metrics, Zero Waste Initiatives
nodes.summary: The page covers APSEZ's waste management practices, including a case study on zero waste to landfill objectives and plastic waste reduction. Waste by category is detailed across FY22-25 for biomedical, battery, e-waste, hazardous, non-hazardous, construction & demolition, and plastic waste. Waste intensity trends from FY18 to FY25 are shown. The project description outlines an Integrated Waste Management System based on the 5Rs. Methodology includes waste source assessment, zero waste to landfill milestones, single-use plastic-free port certification, and a ban on single-use plastics. Outcomes describe the integrated system: collection, segregation, storage, and disposal of dry solid and hazardous waste; recycling of paper, plastic, cardboard, PET bottles, and glass; canteen waste to biogas; and zero waste to landfill achieved at 12 ports.

structure.title: Pursuing innovative practices to improve air quality
structure.summary: The text from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers their efforts to improve air quality by minimizing emissions from fuel combustion, cargo handling, and storage. It outlines their strategic approach, including compliance with legal standards, stakeholder engagement, deployment of innovative dust technologies, and greenbelt development. It details their Environmental Policy and Integrated Management System for combating non-GHG emissions, including monitoring, reporting, and use of the MERCURY software. Specific measures at ports such as retrofitting DG sets, dust suppression systems, and mechanized handling are listed. The text also includes emission data for NOx, SOx, and PM for FY 2022-23 to FY 2024-25, and mentions biodiversity.

structure.title: Protecting biodiversity, restoring our ecosystems
key_items: Alignment with National and International Conservation Association
structure.summary: The text outlines a commitment to biodiversity conservation and sustainable development through an inclusive approach to protecting and sustainably using marine and terrestrial resources. It focuses on ecosystem restoration, responsible mangrove management, biodiversity protection, and reversing land degradation. Guiding principles include an Environmental Policy and Biodiversity Policy promoting a Net Positive Impact and alignment with the Convention on Biological Diversity by 2050. The company is an IBBI signatory and IUCN member, and aligns ports with the Oil Spill Action Plan and NOS-DCP. FY 2024-25 metrics include 4,240 hectares of mangrove afforestation, 1,267 hectares of terrestrial plantation, 11,11,334 KL of wastewater reused, and 4,99,871 square meters of lawn. It also references GRI linkage, material topics, SDGs, and capitals impacted.

structure.title: APSEZ Biodiversity Strategy, Targets, Governance and Performance
key_items: Towards net positive impact on biodiversity by 2050
Our biodiversity strategy; Our biodiversity commitments / targets
structure.summary: This page from Adani Ports and SEZ's 2024-25 Integrated Annual Report outlines its biodiversity agenda. It presents the vision of achieving net positive impact on biodiversity by 2050, with targets including Net Positive Impact and No Net Deforestation by 2050, supported by a Board-ratified Biodiversity Policy and Biodiversity Management Plans. The approach covers progressing from No Net Loss to net gain, alignment with the Post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework, avoidance of eco-sensitive areas, value chain assessments, and supply chain alignment, plus Biodiversity Management Objectives. It details the biodiversity strategy's governance approach—annual stakeholder engagement, a CEO-chaired Sustainability Leadership Committee, Board-level committee, and site-level implementation—alongside long-term and short-term commitments/targets (mangrove and terrestrial plantation), achievements, and biodiversity KPIs from FY2020-21 to FY2024-25.

structure.title: Robust biodiversity risk assessment
structure.summary: Adani Ports and SEZ Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 outlines its robust biodiversity risk assessment as part of sustainability efforts. It details frameworks and standards guiding assessment, including local/national regulations, international best practices (IFC Performance Standards, World Bank EHS Guidelines), and sector-specific guidelines. The scope covers upstream, direct, and downstream operations, identifying risks like habitat disturbance, pollution, and noise. The four-stage assessment process includes preliminary screening using tools like IBAT and ESM, detailed impact assessment via EIS/EIA, formulation of Biodiversity Management Plans for specific ports, and ongoing monitoring. A risk mitigation hierarchy (avoid, reduce, restore, transform) is applied, with examples. The text also provides data on sites assessed, exposed, and managed, covering 15 sites and 13,484.6 hectares.

structure.title: Biodiversity management plan to minimise ecological footprint
structure.summary: The text outlines APSEZ's Biodiversity Management Plan (BMP), a strategic approach to minimize ecological footprint and promote sustainable development. It details measures for conserving species and ecosystems, habitat restoration (e.g., Guneri initiative), sustainable resource use, invasive species management, community engagement, and monitoring and evaluation. The BMP aims to harmonize operations with biodiversity conservation, ensure regulatory compliance, and contribute to global and local biodiversity goals, positioning APSEZ as a leader in sustainable practices.

structure.title: Biodiversity stakeholder engagement
structure.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 section on biodiversity stakeholder engagement covers: a holistic port development approach integrating infrastructure growth with nature conservation for environmental stability and climate resilience; the Adani Group's commitment to plant 100 million trees by 2030 (contribution to 1t.org) with APSEZ planting 3,47,762 trees; strategic collaboration for biodiversity conservation including a biodiversity policy for policy advocacy and dialogue with government, NGOs, and academia, promoting valuation of biodiversity and ecosystem services, a designated biodiversity champion, and IBBI membership; and biodiversity awareness initiatives like the 13th Environment Shikhar (August 8-10, 2024) with 35 employees and expert lectures on CRZ notifications, EIA modeling, port and coastal habitats, terrestrial ecology, and climate change.

structure.title: Key biodiversity conservation initiatives
key_items: Enhancing Mangrove Biodiversity in Kachchh; Location; Location edge
Bio-Shield Projects; Terrestrial Plantation; Project Summary; Community-Based Initiatives; Project Summary
structure.summary: The text details Adani Ports and SEZ Limited's FY 2024-25 biodiversity conservation initiatives. It covers coastal biodiversity enhancement in Kachchh through mangrove restoration, including seed sowing, survival rates, and macrofaunal increase. It describes bio-shield projects at Dahej, Hazira, and Tuna using mangroves and local species to protect coastlines and generate income. Terrestrial plantation efforts include the Guneri restoration project and the 'Adani Van' initiative. Community-based initiatives like Vruksh Se Vikas and multi-species mangrove plantation in Kandla are highlighted, emphasizing community participation and ecological restoration.

structure.title: Conservation of olive ridley sea turtles (lepidochelys olivacea) in Odisha
key_items: Vessel movement; Our Efforts have Contributed to Encouraging Results
Our Efforts have Contributed to Encouraging Results
structure.summary: The text covers the conservation of olive ridley sea turtles in Odisha, including their presence in coastal deltaic regions with mangroves, migration from October to May, and mass nesting (arribada) behavior. It details threats such as habitat loss, light pollution, fishing activities, predation, and vessel movement. Key nesting areas like the Dhamra, Devi, and Rushikulya river mouths are identified, noting that ~50% of the global and 90% of the Indian population nests there, with nesting starting in March. Conservation efforts include the Gahirmatha Marine Wildlife Sanctuary, no fishing zones, Turtle Excluder Devices, patrolling, community engagement, and specific activities by Gopalpur and Dhamra Ports. Results show average nesting of 4.02 lakhs at Rushikulya and 4.38 lakhs at Gahirmatha over three years.

structure.title: Future strategy in biodiversity conservation
key_items: Biodiversity Conservations & Restorations Across all the Operational Sites
structure.summary: This text from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers biodiversity conservation and restoration across operational sites. It lists specific locations (Tuna, Mundra, Dahej, Dighi, Murmugao, Hazira, Vizhinjam, Karaikal, Gopalpur, Krishnapatnam, Kattupalli, Ennore, Dhamra, Gangavaram) with hectare figures for various initiatives. Conservation types include mangrove afforestation and conservation, terrestrial afforestation, grassland restoration, multi-species mangrove biodiversity parks, Miyawaki plantation, multi-species plantation, bio-shield projects, turtle conservation programmes, and Kanika Island conservation. Future strategies are outlined: expanding mangrove restoration, green census surveys, biodiversity parks, carbon sequestration projects, massive plantation drives, awareness and knowledge building, and turtle conservation programmes.

structure.title: Oil spill prevention and management
structure.summary: The text details APSEZ's Oil Spill Prevention and Management plan from its Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, aligned with NOS-DCP and IPIECA standards. It covers a Tier-1 oil spill contingency plan addressing accident scenarios and vulnerable areas, regularly updated, with a modelling study showing a 700-tonne spill spreading 400 metres in four hours. APSEZ's resources include dispersants, absorbent pads, storage tanks, pumps, containment booms, skimmers, and towing equipment. The plan covers spill scenarios during anchoring, berthing, and cargo handling, plus land spill management. It includes regular maintenance, inspections, and a 7-point action plan for leak-proof containers, hazardous waste storage, stacking, tarpaulins, first-aid kits, inspections, and training. Performance metrics show zero spills achieved in FY 2024-25.

structure.title: APSEZ Workforce Demographics and People Strategy Overview
structure.summary: This page from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 presents workforce demographic data across several sections: Age Group (393 under 30, 599 aged 30-50, and 2,220 over 50); Management Level (11 Top, 67 Senior, 330 Middle, 762 Junior, and 2,042 Supervisory/Technician employees); Nationality (3,212 Asian Indian employees); and Gender (3,133 male and 79 female employees). The page additionally lists report navigation sections: Portfolio Overview, Corporate Overview, Strategic Review, ESG Overview, Statutory Reports, and Financial Statements.

structure.title: Investing in People Training & Development
structure.summary: The text details APSEZ's investment in employee training and development through continuous learning, a talent development approach to avoid obsolescence, and a learning culture. It describes the Capability Building and Leadership Development framework supported by the Adani Behavioural Competency Framework, mentorship, cross-functional knowledge sharing, and the e-Vidyalaya-Percipio platform for training in risk management, soft skills, and compliance. Key initiatives include the Adani Accelerated Leadership Programme (AALP) with 12 participants from IIT/IIM/MDI, a Knowledge Sharing & Mentoring Programme using the 70:20:10 model over 18-24 months with 13 completions, the Human Potential Programme with IIT/IIM faculty and industrial excursions, e-learning for non-managers, and the Adani Krishnapatnam Skill Development Centre (ASDC) with 21 simulation programs. It also lists maritime sector programmes: RTG crane operator training for Indian and Tanzanian students, HMV driving training, and marine engine/dredging training. Training data includes man-hours by age group, gender, management level, and training type, along with 100% employee training coverage and mandays training for FTEs and total workforce.

structure.summary: APSEZ's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 page covers talent management, learning and development, performance management, job rotations, and leadership development. It details the Adani Accelerated Leadership Programme (AALP) with 12 AALPs from IIT, IIM, and MDI; the Knowledge Sharing & Mentoring Programme (70:20:10 model, 18–24 months, 13 completions); the Human Potential Programme with IIT/IIM faculty and industry excursions; Training for Non-Managers via eVidyalaya–Percipio; the new 20-acre Adani Krishnapatnam Skill Development Centre with 21 simulation programmes; and key maritime programmes (RTG crane operator training for Indian and Tanzanian students, HMV driving, marine engine/dredging training). nodes.title: Performance-Linked Compensation Framework
key_items: Performance-Linked Compensation Structure; E2 to E4 Grades
nodes.summary: The text outlines APSEZ's performance-linked compensation framework, which promotes meritocracy and equal pay. It details a tiered structure by employee grade: O1-E1 receive 10% of CTC as performance incentives, E2-E4 receive 15%, and GM and above are evaluated on organizational and individual performance, including ESG metrics. A 4-point scale is used, with qualitative adjustments for ESG and safety for senior management. Executive compensation is linked to ESG performance, covering compliance, human rights, financial targets, risk management, IT, cyber security, and customer satisfaction. Performance pay splits 70% individual (including ESG) and 30% organizational (50% revenue, 25% EBITDA, 25% RoCE). The company commits to equal pay regardless of gender, with periodic reviews and NRC oversight of executive remuneration. CEO compensation includes fixed salary, variable pay, and long-term incentives tied to financial and ESG indicators. Wage data by management level and gender, pay ratios, and compensation benchmarking via AON are also included.

nodes.title: Employee Support Programmes
key_items: Emotional Intelligence (EI) Programme; Medical Interventions; Flexible Working Hours/Work from Home; Childcare Facilities or Contributions; Welfare Facilities
nodes.summary: The text outlines APSEZ's Employee Support Programmes centered on well-being and work-life balance. Initiatives include Workplace Stress Management with a 4-month wellness journey for senior leadership; an Emotional Intelligence Programme for campus cadres; Sport & Health Initiatives like virtual yoga and sports events; Medical Interventions with health facilities, check-ups, and insurance; Flexible Working Hours/Work from Home with a 48-hour work week limit; Childcare Facilities including scholarships and loan subsidies; Welfare Facilities such as retirement benefits, loans, and marriage gifts; Paid Parental Leaves with creche facilities; and Benefits data on parental leave entitlement, uptake, return-to-work, and retention rates for male and female employees.

nodes.title: Employee Turnover Rate
nodes.summary: The text presents APSEZ's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 employee turnover data: involuntary and voluntary workforce turnover numbers by Indian region (North, Central, East, West, South, Northeastern) and voluntary rates by age group (<30, 30-50, >50), gender (male/female), and management level (top, senior, middle, junior, supervisory/technician), with percentages. It covers periodic Gallup assessment surveys evaluating 15 attributes to structure interactions (casual conversations, meeting agendas, performance evaluations, team goal-setting), an assessment score of 7.9 versus an 8.4 target for FY 2024-25, and employee survey aspects including Employee Net Promoter Score, total employees covered, job experience, happiness, purpose, and stress management.

nodes.title: Freedom of Association
nodes.summary: The text highlights the company's commitment to freedom of association, including employees' rights to form and join trade unions, negotiate, and participate in collective bargaining without intimidation or retaliation. It notes that 100% of the workforce is covered by collective bargaining agreements in FY24 and FY25, and lists key topics covered in these agreements such as health and safety, CSR, fair remuneration, working hours, skill development, career progression, flexibility, lifelong learning, stress management, and equal opportunities. The document also includes ESG overview, statutory reports, financial statements, and human rights references, with a rating of 7.9 on a 0-10 scale and multiple 4.0 ratings on a 5-scale for both years.

structure.title: Protecting human rights
structure.summary: The section covers APSEZ's comprehensive human rights framework, aligned with UN and ILO principles, including policies, monitoring, and due diligence across employees, suppliers, communities, and value chains. It details supply chain assessments, key risks (forced labor, child labor, fair wages, health and safety, harassment, discrimination), grievance mechanisms, and remedial actions. It highlights zero incidents in FY 2024-25, 86% employee training, 67% supplier assessment, and governance structures. It also addresses escalation processes for discrimination and harassment, community and security personnel safeguards, M&A due diligence, and occupational health and safety commitments with a zero-harm approach, ISO 45001 certification, and key safety metrics.

nodes.title: Comprehensive Human Rights Policy & Guidelines
key_items: Human Rights Policy Effectiveness Monitoring Process
nodes.summary: The text outlines APSEZ's commitment to human rights protection, aligned with Adani Group's vision and international standards (UN Guiding Principles, ILO Declaration). It details a comprehensive Human Rights Policy, strategy, and due diligence process covering employees, suppliers, communities, and value chains. Key performance metrics for FY 2024-25 are provided, showing zero incidents of discrimination, child labor, forced labor, and human rights risks at sites, with 86% employee training completion and 67% supplier assessment. The monitoring process includes grievance mechanisms, audits, fact-finding, corrective measures, and review. The due diligence process involves risk identification, SAQs, heightened due diligence in conflict zones, and oversight by committees. Indigenous communities are respected, and no adverse impacts were reported.

nodes.title: APSEZ Human Rights Policy Monitoring and Due Diligence
key_items: Integrated Human Rights Policies; Due Diligence Processes; Remedial Actions; Transparency in Communication; Stakeholder Engagement
nodes.summary: The page details APSEZ's human rights framework, including a monitoring process (information gathering, indicators, fact-finding, preventive/corrective measures, review). It outlines a strategic approach aligned with UN and ILO principles, covering integrated policies, due diligence, remedial actions, transparency, and stakeholder engagement. It describes comprehensive due diligence across operations and value chain, including pre-merger assessments, committee oversight, ERM integration, periodic reviews, and self-assessment questionnaires. It also covers heightened due diligence in conflict situations and a six-step risk assessment process, with examples like security check-ins and survey participation.

nodes.title: Safeguarding Human Rights Across the Supply Chain
nodes.summary: This text from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 outlines their commitment to safeguarding human rights across the supply chain. It details an annual supplier assessment process aligned with their Supplier Code of Conduct, including risk assessment, auditing high-risk facilities, capacity-building training, and multi-stakeholder collaboration. The Human Rights Assessment Process focuses on identifying risk areas and formulating mitigation plans. It presents statistics on the percentage of sites reviewed, risks with mitigation actions, and total assessed sites with identified risks across own operations, contractors and Tier 1 suppliers, and joint ventures over the last three years, noting that no human rights risks were identified in FY 2024-25.

It defines each issue, lists indicators, potential value chain impacts and vulnerable groups, and cites relevant policies. Prevention strategies are detailed, including responsible recruitment, supplier engagement, legal compliance, training, grievance mechanisms, and audits. It describes governance structures like the Group Monitoring Committee and Grievance Redressal Committees, their roles in policy oversight, monitoring, and handling complaints, and notes that 86% of employees received human rights training in FY 2024-25.

nodes.title: Escalation Process for Discrimination and Harassment Incidents
key_items: Mitigation Processes; Mitigation Processes; Mitigation Processes; Mitigation Processes; Mitigation Processes
nodes.summary: The text covers APSEZ's grievance management system for discrimination and harassment, including reporting channels like website, complaint boxes, and a dedicated email, ensuring confidentiality and fair resolution for all stakeholders. It details mitigation and remediation plans for local communities (cultural heritage, land acquisition standards, no indigenous people), workforce (human rights training, POSH, code of conduct, grievance mechanisms, induction), security personnel (specialized human rights training, no violations, 80% trained in FY24-25), value chain (supplier code of conduct, due diligence, corrective actions, independent assessments), and mergers & acquisitions (due diligence, UN Guiding Principles, mitigation plans at three sites).

nodes.title: Remedial Actions for Human Rights Risk Mitigation
nodes.summary: The text outlines remedial actions for human rights risk mitigation, including expanding the risk management framework with sub-committees, strengthening governance with independent directors, broadening risk identification to new business engagements, implementing rigorous ESG due diligence for offshore M&A and greenfield projects, conducting community/supplier/customer surveys, and performing systematic reviews and stakeholder engagement. It also details occupational health and safety (OHS) commitments: a structured OHS policy, zero-compromise approach, alignment with global standards, consequence management policy, safety management system manual, safety motto and target of zero harm and 25% LTI reduction by 2025, and behavior correction techniques.

nodes.title: Committed to workers’ health, wellbeing & safety
nodes.summary: This section outlines APSEZ's commitment to worker health, well-being, and safety through a zero-compromise approach anchored in its OHS Policy and 'Zero Harm, Zero Injuries, Zero Excuses' motto. It details the Safety Management System manual (Safety Bible), governance framework, ISO 45001 certification, and the 5C Model for safety culture. It covers 2026 zero-harm goals, progress against 2025 targets, training programs, contractor safety management, process safety measures, well-being initiatives, and technology-enabled OHS monitoring. It also addresses the Oil Spill Contingency Plan, logistics and road safety, automated OHS systems, and recognition programs, highlighting key FY 2024-25 metrics such as LTIFR of 0.29 and over 27 lakh safety training man-hours.

nodes.title: Zero-Compromise Approach to Workplace Safety
nodes.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 section on Occupational Health & Safety outlines the company's commitment to worker health, well-being, and safety through a structured OHS Policy prioritizing prevention of work-related illnesses and injuries. It details a zero-compromise approach to workplace safety, including materiality assessments, alignment with international standards, adherence to global best practices, risk management, stakeholder engagement, and compliance with national regulations and Good International Industrial Practices. The text also covers a rewards and recognition program for employees, a Board-ratified Consequence Management Policy addressing positive and negative outcomes with severe penalties for safety failures, and the company's safety motto: 'Zero Harm, Zero Injuries, and Zero Excuses.'

nodes.title: Our Safety Bible
nodes.summary: The text outlines Adani's Safety Management System manual, covering OHS policies at group, business, and site levels, safety governance, Felt Leadership, SOPs, RACI, goals, and 10 Life Saving Safety Rules. It targets zero harm and a 25% LTI reduction by 2025 from a 2016 baseline. It details roles for employees, associates, and vendors, and mentions Suraksha-Samwaad as a behavior correction technique. Key FY 2024-25 highlights include LTIFR of 0.29, 27,44,654 safety training man-hours, OHS policy implementation, ISO 45001:2018 certification at all sites, robust OHS governance, six active Safety Task Forces, material topics M8, M9, M12, SDG alignment, GRI linkage, and impacts on human and social/relationship capital.

nodes.title: Robust OHS governance framework
key_items: Promoting Excellence in OHS; Regular Risk Assessment
Modelled Around a Robust Safety Proposition; The 5C Model
Modelled Around a Robust Safety Proposition
nodes.summary: The text outlines APSEZ's robust OHS governance framework, covering all manufacturing locations and workforce, with a commitment to continuous improvement. It details ISO 45001 certification, regular OHS programs, PDCA cycle deployment, internal inspections and audits, risk prioritization and redressal, and key levers of OHS management including audits and incident investigation. It promotes excellence through policies, risk assessments, training, incident reporting, health and wellness programs, performance indicators, emergency response plans, audits, employee engagement, stakeholder collaboration, and the Suraksha Samwaad behavior system. The 5C Model (Commitment, Capability, Conformance, Communication, Culture) is described as a strategic framework to enhance safety culture and performance, with ongoing evaluation to maintain world-class safety standards.

nodes.title: 2026 Goals – Towards Zero Harm
nodes.summary: The section covers APSEZ's 2026 safety goals and zero-harm vision, detailing an ISO 45001:2018 certified OHS governance structure with multi-tiered councils and committees. It reviews progress toward 2025 safety and health targets, including leadership engagement, contractor training, audits, and CAPA deployment. Safety initiatives include the Contractor Incubation Series (Saksham, Samwaad) and skilling campaigns (Urja, Upkaran, Unchai, Rescue), plus process safety measures like QRA, HAZOP, and PSM. Employee and contractor well-being programs, hazard identification, and technology monitoring are described. The section also covers awards, recognition items, and joint management-worker safety committees with site-specific customization and training.

nodes.title: Robust OHS Governance Structure Promoting Safety
nodes.summary: APSEZ outlines its 2026 safety goals and comprehensive OHS governance framework aimed at zero harm. The text details the ISO 45001:2018 certified Safety Management System and a multi-tiered governance model comprising Safety Steering Council, Business Safety Council, Site Safety Councils, and Safety Task Forces, each with defined roles from corporate to site level. It describes safety committee representation across board, corporate, business, management, and non-management levels, including meeting frequencies. The document also covers safety initiatives, implementation strategies, and stakeholder engagement involving employees, contractors, third parties, business partners, and communities.

nodes.title: Outcome towards 2025 safety and health targets: Elevating our safety commitments
nodes.summary: The text outlines progress toward 2025 safety and health targets, including monitoring and assessment for improvement, programs to minimize incidents and foster safety culture. It details leadership participation in safety engagement (PSAP), contractor induction and Saksham training, reward and recognition policy, improvements in SRFA audits, structural stability studies, Samwaad to reduce unsafe acts, CAPA deployment, task force KPI scorecards, and LPSE learnings. Benefits include KRAs, capacity building, engagement, safe workplace, VSR elimination, and proactive prevention. Status updates cover PSAP interactions, Saksham participants, rewards, SRFA audits, electrical safety, VSR audits, UA/hr achievement, CAPA execution, SSC/BSSC meetings, and LPSE training with project executions.

nodes.title: Safety Initiatives, Skilling Campaigns and Process Safety at APSEZ
key_items: Progressing in the Area of Process Safety
nodes.summary: The page covers APSEZ's safety initiatives including the Contractor Incubation Series with Saksham (3D animated experience-based learning for worker safety) and Samwaad (worker participation platform via Adani GENSUITE for reporting safety concerns within 40 seconds, anonymously). Safety skilling campaigns include Urja (electrical safety, 5E Model), Upkaran (safe lifting, 5L Model), Unchai (working at heights, 5C Model), and Rescue (emergency response), with 59 campaigns and 3,088 man-hours in FY 2024-25. Process safety covers QRA, HAZID, HAZOP, PSM, PSSR, HIRA for new and existing processes, and independent consultant gap assessments. Employee and contractor well-being includes emergency healthcare, medical assessments, health data management, dedicated doctors, and hazard identification processes (third-party assessments, monthly self-assessments, vulnerability risk assessments, SRFA). Major process safety initiatives include tech monitoring via CCTV, safety awareness, safety alerts and CAPAs, and monthly reward and recognition.

nodes.title: Awards and Joint Safety Committees in APSEZ Report
key_items: Joint Committees to Promote Safety Culture
nodes.summary: The page covers APSEZ's awards, listing gifts like computers, bicycles, refrigerators, washing machines, and LED TVs, and a gold-coloured helmet with a Safety Star Logo. It details joint management-worker health and safety committees with site-specific customization, equal representation, frequent meetings for OHS reviews and goal-setting, transparent minutes sharing, training for committee members, consultant resources, and record-keeping for accountability. Also references portfolio, corporate, ESG, statutory, and financial sections.

The Oil Spill Contingency Plan covers up to 700 tonnes, with management structure, shoreline mapping, equipment procurement, storage, response strategy, fire safety, training, drills, and communication. The OHS framework expands to logistics, warehouse, and road safety, integrates OHS into procurement via Ariba, and includes contractor safety management, stop-work authority, audio-visual tools, and workers' rights. Key initiatives cover road safety, infrastructure, training, and emergency response, with 1,87,540 contractors trained.

structure.title: Emergency preparedness and response
structure.summary: The text covers Adani Ports and SEZ Limited's emergency preparedness and response plan, including fire safety measures, response processes for disasters, simulation exercises, and coverage of all port operations. It details the security framework with drone technology, patrolling, maritime collaboration with the Indian Coast Guard, and joint exercises like Sagar Kawach. It also reports OHS performance for FY 2024-25, highlighting data-driven safety insights from 123,164 reported concerns via the Adani GENSUITE platform, and notes six contractor fatalities with investigations and shared lessons to prevent recurrence.

structure.title: Fatalities by Year
