structure.title: Lease Liabilities and Other Financial Liabilities Notes
structure.summary: The page presents Notes 15 and 16 from Adani Ports' consolidated financial statements. Note 15 (Lease Liabilities, continued) provides a maturity table of future minimum lease payments, finance charges, and present value for March 31, 2025 and 2024, categorized as within one year, one to five years, and more than five years. Note 16 (Other Financial Liabilities) discloses non-current and current portions as of both dates, listing items such as derivative instruments, capital creditors, employee payables, unpaid dividends, interest accrued, customer deposits, business combination payables, and put option liability. A footnote explains the reclassification of employee payables for better presentation under Ind AS 1. All amounts are in crore.

structure.title: 16 Other financial liabilities (Contd.)
structure.summary: The text presents consolidated financial statement notes for the year ended March 31, 2025. Note 16 covers other financial liabilities, specifically the Ind AS 7 disclosure of changes in liabilities from financing activities, showing reconciliations for borrowings, lease liabilities, unpaid dividends, and derivative contracts across cash flows, foreign exchange, lease additions, profit/loss charges, dividends, and acquisitions. Note 17 details other liabilities split into non-current and current portions, listing advances, deposits, statutory liabilities, unearned income, deferred income, government grants, unearned revenue, and contract liabilities. It also includes movements in deferred government grants and describes the grant's composition, including Viability Gap Funding for Vizhinjam Seaport and EPCG scheme benefits, plus a note on contract liabilities.

structure.title: March 31, 2025 March 31, 2024
structure.summary: This section of the consolidated financial statements covers Notes 17 through 21, comparing figures as of March 31, 2025, and 2024. Note 17 details other liabilities, including advances, deposits, statutory liabilities, unearned income, deferred income, government grants (with a movement schedule for deferred government grants), and contract liabilities. Note 18 presents current borrowings, including foreign currency letters of credit, current maturities of non-current borrowings, and short-term borrowings from banks and others, with notes on interest rates, security, repayment terms, and subsidiary-specific loans. Note 19 covers trade payables, distinguishing MSME and other creditors, with ageing schedules, and Note 20 details provisions for employee benefits and asset retirement obligations, including movement. Note 21 presents revenue from operations, breaking down revenue from contracts with customers and reconciling contract price to revenue recognized.

nodes.title: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements: Other Liabilities
nodes.summary: This page presents Note 17, Other Liabilities, from the consolidated financial statements. It details non-current and current portions, listing items such as advances from customers, deposits, statutory liabilities, unearned income, deferred income, government grants, unearned revenue, and contract liabilities. Comparative figures for March 31, 2025, and 2024, are provided. Notes include a movement schedule for Deferred Government Grant (opening balance, additions, amortization, closing balance) and a description of the grant's main components, including Kerala Viability Gap Funding and EPCG scheme benefits. Contract liabilities are explained as advances for services and unsatisfied performance obligations for storage and dispatch services.

nodes.title: Particulars
nodes.summary: This note details current borrowings as of March 31, 2025, with comparative figures for 2024, including foreign currency letters of credit (secured/unsecured), current maturities of non-current borrowings, and short-term borrowings from banks (secured/unsecured) and others. It lists amounts for each category and provides notes on interest rates, security, repayment terms, and subsidiary loans, covering term loans, bill discounting, letters of credit, and facilities from various banks, along with repayments during the year.

nodes.title: Notes:
nodes.summary: This section of the consolidated financial statements presents Note 18 on Current Borrowings as of March 31, 2025, comparing figures to March 31, 2024. It tabulates various borrowings including foreign currency letters of credit (secured/unsecured), current maturities of non-current borrowings, and short-term borrowings from banks (secured/unsecured) and others, with amounts in crore. Detailed notes describe each borrowing type: repaid rupee term loans, interest rates (e.g., Repo Rate plus spread, 3M T Bill plus spread, SOFR-linked), security details (charges on assets, pledge of equity shares), repayment terms, and subsidiary-specific loans (Adani Krishnapatnam Port, AYN Logistics, Adani Hazira Port, Colombo West International Terminal, Dhamra Port Company, Tanzania East Africa Gateway Terminal).

nodes.title: 19 Trade Payables
nodes.summary: Note 19 presents trade payables as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, distinguishing MSME and other creditors, including related party dues. It provides ageing schedules for both years, categorizing amounts by due status and buckets from less than 1 year to more than 3 years, with separate lines for disputed MSME and other dues. Note 20 covers provisions, split into non-current and current portions. Non-current provisions include employee benefits (gratuity and compensated absences) and asset retirement obligation. Current provisions are also detailed. A note shows the movement of asset retirement obligation from opening to closing balance.

nodes.title: 21 Revenue from Operations
nodes.summary: The text presents Note 21 'Revenue from Operations' for fiscal years ending March 31, 2025, and 2024, with figures in crore. It breaks down revenue from contracts with customers, including income from operations (port infrastructure services) and lease, upfront premium, and deferred infrastructure income, totaling 30,475.33 crore and 26,710.56 crore. It also provides a reconciliation of revenue recognized with contract price, showing contract price, adjustments for change in consideration refund liability, contract assets, and contract liabilities, resulting in revenue from contract with customers of 30,083.03 crore and 26,157.02 crore.

structure.title: 21 Revenue from Operations (Contd.)
key_items: c) Assets given under operating lease
structure.summary: The text covers revenue from operations notes for Adani Ports and SEZ Limited's consolidated financial statements for FY 2024-25. It details finance lease agreements: non-cancellable, no contingent rent or restrictions, land lease rent revision up to 20% every 3 years, and one-time non-refundable upfront premium (₹2500-4500/sq m) with income of ₹16.85 crore (previous year ₹20.12 crore including ₹Nil upfront premium vs ₹17.80 crore). It also covers operating leases: renewable land leases, subsidiary agreements with FCI for DBFOO warehousing with revenue based on Annual Guaranteed Tonnage, future minimum lease rentals receivable (₹2,257.11 crore total as of March 31, 2025, and ₹2,048.96 crore as of March 31, 2024, with breakdowns by maturity), and operating lease income of ₹140.22 crore (previous year ₹168.61 crore).

structure.title: 22 Other Income
structure.summary: The text presents financial statement notes for the year ended March 31, 2025, comparing figures with March 31, 2024. Note 22 details Other Income, including interest income from various sources, finance lease, gains on liability extinguishment and sale of investments, dividend, scrap sales, profit on asset sales, unclaimed liabilities, FVTPL gains, financial guarantee income, government grant amortization, and miscellaneous income, totaling ₹1,304.48 crore and ₹1,499.42 crore for 2025 and 2024. Note 23 lists operating expenses such as cargo handling, customer claims, railway charges, tug and pilotage, maintenance dredging, repairs, stores, sub-lease land cost, power and fuel, waterfront charges, finance lease asset transfers, freight, aircraft expenses, customs, establishment, and service concession construction costs. Note 24 covers employee benefits: salaries, provident fund, gratuity, and staff welfare. Note 25 details finance costs, including interest on debentures, loans, lease liabilities, bank charges, derivative gains, and foreign exchange losses.

structure.title: Notes 23-25: Operating Expenses, Employee Benefits, Finance Costs
structure.summary: The page presents three notes to the consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, with comparative figures for March 31, 2024, in crore. Note 23, Operating Expenses, itemizes cargo handling, customer claims, railway service charges, tug and pilotage, maintenance dredging, repairs, stores, sub-lease land cost, power and fuel, waterfront charges, finance lease asset transfers, freight and transportation, aircraft operating expenses, customs, establishment, and service concession construction expenses, with totals. Note 24, Employee Benefits Expense, lists salaries, wages and bonus, provident and other funds, gratuity, and staff welfare. Note 25, Finance Costs, details interest and bank charges, interest on debentures and bonds, loans and buyer's credit, lease liabilities, other interest, bank charges, gain on derivatives/swaps, and foreign exchange loss, with totals.

structure.title: Other Expenses and Income Tax Notes
structure.summary: The page presents notes to the consolidated financial statements of Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited for the year ended March 31, 2025. It includes section 26 'Other Expenses', which lists various expense particulars such as rent, rates and taxes, insurance, advertisement, repairs, legal and professional fees, corporate support service fees, IT support, security, communication, electric power, travel, directors' sitting fees, commission to non-executive directors, charity and donations, inventory diminution, and miscellaneous expenses, with corresponding amounts for March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024, totaling ₹1,975.55 crore and ₹1,833.90 crore respectively. Section 27 'Income Tax' begins by stating that the major components of income tax expenses for the same periods are presented below, though the detailed breakdown is not included in the provided text.

structure.title: (i) Tax Expense reported in the Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss
structure.summary: The text presents a detailed breakdown of tax expenses reported in the Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. It includes current income tax charges, adjustments for earlier years, deferred tax related to temporary differences, and tax credits under the Minimum Alternative Tax. It also covers exceptional items, such as deferred and current tax on the write-off of past MAT credit due to the election of a new tax regime. Additionally, it lists tax impacts on Other Comprehensive Income items, including cash flow hedges, defined benefit plans, and FVTOCI equity investments. The figures are in crore.

structure.title: (ii) Balance Sheet Section
structure.summary: The text presents balance sheet tax items—net taxes recoverable and current tax liabilities for March 31, 2025 and 2024—with a note on year-wise balances. It then provides a reconciliation of tax expenses with accounting profit multiplied by India's statutory tax rate of 34.94%, detailing profit before tax, tax effect adjustments (e.g., disallowed expenses, Chapter VI-A deductions, joint venture profit share, special provisions, exempt income, prior-year adjustments, indexation, MAT credit, deferred tax rate changes, unrecognized tax losses, subsidiary tax rates, dividend elimination, and others), and concludes with reported income tax and effective tax rate.

structure.title: (iv) Deferred Tax Liability (net)
structure.summary: The text presents Note 27 on Income Tax from the consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It details the components of net deferred tax liability and assets, listing items such as accelerated depreciation, employee benefits provisions, unrealised intra-group profits, fair valuation gains from subsidiary stake dilution, unabsorbed losses/depreciation, finance lease receivables, preference share debt components, guarantees, deemed investments, business combination adjustments, SCA receivables/intangible assets, equity investments at FVTOCI, upfront infrastructure income, transaction costs of a composite scheme, forex impacts, impairment provisions, MAT credit entitlement, and other adjustments. Corresponding amounts in crores are provided for the balance sheet as at March 31, 2025 and 2024, and for the statement of profit and loss for the same periods.

structure.title: (v) Deferred Tax reflected in the Balance Sheet as follows
structure.summary: The text is from the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 of Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited, Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, specifically note 27 on Income Tax. It presents the deferred tax reflected in the balance sheet as deferred tax assets (net) and deferred tax liabilities (net) for March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024, including components such as tax credit entitlement under MAT and deferred tax liabilities (net). It provides figures in crore for deferred tax assets, liabilities, and net amounts for both years. It also states that MAT credit of ₹390.64 crore (previous year ₹499.91 crore) was recognised during the year.

structure.title: (vi) The Group has following unutilised MAT credit under the Income Tax Act, 1961 for which deferred tax asset has been recognised in the Balance Sheet
structure.summary: The text details the Group's tax-related items: (vi) unutilised MAT credit under the Income Tax Act, 1961, with amounts and expiry years, for which deferred tax assets are recognised; (vii) certain subsidiaries' carried-forward unabsorbed depreciation (no expiry) and carried-forward losses (expiring within 8 years), including a table of loss expiry amounts, and notes that deferred tax assets are not recognised for these losses due to uncertainty of recoverability; and (viii) deferred income taxes are not provided on undistributed earnings of subsidiaries expected not to be distributed in the foreseeable future.

structure.title: 28 Earnings Per Share (EPS)
structure.summary: The text presents two notes to consolidated financial statements for Adani Ports and SEZ Limited for FY2024-25. Note 28 details Earnings Per Share (EPS), showing profit attributable to equity holders, net profit for EPS calculation, weighted average shares, and basic/diluted EPS for March 31, 2025 and 2024. Note 29 covers Ind AS-19 employee benefits, including defined contribution plan expenses (provident fund and superannuation), and defined gratuity plan details: plan description, changes in present value of defined benefit obligation, changes in fair value of plan assets, net asset/liability recognized in balance sheet, and expense recognized in profit and loss, with comparative figures for both years.

structure.title: Ind AS 19 Employee Benefits Disclosures: OCI, Assumptions, Plan Assets, Sensitivity
key_items: (v) Recognised in the other comprehensive income
structure.summary: The page presents disclosures under Ind AS 19 for employee benefits, covering: (v) amounts recognised in other comprehensive income, including actuarial gains/losses from demographic and financial assumptions, experience variance, capitalised amounts, and return on plan assets; (vi) principal assumptions for gratuity obligations such as discount rate, salary escalation, mortality, and attrition, with explanatory notes on salary increases and expected return on assets; (vii) major categories of plan assets as a percentage of fair value, noting investments with insurer and unavailability of underlying details; and (viii) the sensitivity analysis method, based on reasonably possible changes in assumptions while holding others constant.

structure.title: Quantitative sensitivity analysis for significant assumption is as below
structure.summary: The text presents a quantitative sensitivity analysis of defined benefit obligations for March 31, 2025 and 2024, showing impacts of changes in discount rate, salary growth rate, attrition rate, and mortality rate. It includes a maturity profile of the obligation with weighted average duration (6 years in 2025, 7 years in 2024) and expected future payments within specified time buckets, along with total expected payments. It also states the expected contribution to the gratuity fund for FY 2025-26 (₹155.07 crore) compared to the previous year (₹206.30 crore).

structure.title: Employee Benefit Disclosures: Sensitivity, Maturity and Expected Contributions
key_items: (x) The Following payments are expected contributions to the defined benefit plan in future years:
structure.summary: This page presents Ind AS 19 employee benefit disclosures, including sensitivity analysis of defined benefit obligations to changes in discount rate, salary growth, attrition, and mortality for March 31, 2025 and 2024, with impacts in crore. It also provides the maturity profile showing weighted average duration of 6 and 7 years, and expected future contributions to the defined benefit plan across time buckets (next 12 months, 2-5 years, 6-10 years, beyond 10 years) with total expected payments for both years, plus a note on the Group's expected gratuity fund contribution for FY 2025-26.

structure.title: Employee Benefit Asset-Liability Matching and Segment Information Disclosures
structure.summary: The page covers Ind AS-19 employee benefit disclosures on asset-liability matching strategies, detailing a purchased insurance policy that mitigates liquidity risk but exposes the Group to interest rate risk due to shorter asset duration. It also presents segment information under Ind AS 108, identifying reportable segments as Port and SEZ activities and others (aircraft operating income, warehousing, container train services, logistics). It describes segment identification by the chief operating decision maker, segment revenue and results treatment of unallocable items, and segment assets and liabilities composition with unallocable common items.

structure.title: Inter Segment transfer:
structure.summary: The text outlines inter-segment transfer accounting, noting revenue recognition at market-based sales prices with group-level elimination of profit or loss. It presents a segment information summary covering revenue (external, inter-segment, total), results (segment results, unallocated corporate income, operating profit, finance expense, interest income, profit before exceptional items and tax, exceptional items, tax expense, profit after tax, non-controlling interest, net profit), and other information (segment assets, unallocated corporate assets), with figures for Port and SEZ activities, Others, Eliminations, and Total in crore for the year ended March 31, 2025.

structure.title: Segment Information Summary with Profit and Assets
key_items: Summary of segment information is given below:
structure.summary: The page presents a summary of segment information, including revenue breakdown (external and inter-segment sales), segment results, unallocated corporate income, operating profit, finance expense, interest income, profit before tax, exceptional items, tax expense, profit after tax, non-controlling interest, net profit, segment assets, and unallocated corporate assets. It provides detailed financial figures for Port and SEZ activities, others, eliminations, and total, covering comparative data for two periods.

structure.title: Segment Information: Port/SEZ and Geographic Segment Disclosures
key_items: Additional information regarding the Company's geographical segments:
structure.summary: The page presents segment information from the consolidated financial statements, covering Port and SEZ activities and Others, with eliminations and totals. It includes assets classified as held for sale, total assets, segment liabilities, unallocated corporate liabilities, liabilities associated with held-for-sale assets, total liabilities, capital expenditure, depreciation and amortisation, major non-cash expenses, and impairment loss. It also provides additional geographical segment information for India and Outside India, showing non-current assets and revenue from external customers for current and previous years. A note states no single external customer accounts for 10% or more of group revenue. Previous year figures are in italics.

structure.title: 31 Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited’s share in the voting power of subsidiary/ Step down subsidiary companies as at year end is as follows:
structure.summary: The text is a note to consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, listing Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's share in the voting power of 26 subsidiary and step-down subsidiary companies as of year-end. It includes the name of each company, country of incorporation (India or Australia), and proportion of ownership interest for March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. The list covers logistics, aviation, SEZ, port terminals, airports, infrastructure, warehousing, hospitals, dredging, and other entities, with ownership percentages ranging from 49% to 100%, and includes references to specific notes and a subsidiary disposed of during the year.

structure.title: 31 Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited’s share in the voting power of subsidiary/ Step down subsidiary companies as at year end is as follows: (Contd.)
structure.summary: This text is an excerpt from the Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, specifically Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It presents a continued list (Sr. No. 27 to 58) of the company's share in the voting power of its subsidiary and step-down subsidiary companies as at year end. The list includes various entities such as Mundra Crude Oil Terminal Limited, Marine Infrastructure Developer Private Limited, several Adani Agri Logistics subsidiaries across different locations, Adani Bulk Terminals (Mundra) Limited, Adani Warehousing Limited, Dhamra Infrastructure Limited, Adani Logistics Services Limited, Adani Noble Limited, and Adani Forwarding Agent Limited.

structure.title: Country of Incorporation
structure.summary: This document lists subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries of Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited, detailing for each: serial number, company name, country of incorporation (India, Singapore, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Israel, UAE, Tanzania, Oman), proportion of ownership interest for March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024, and notes on acquisitions, incorporations, strike-offs, or references. It includes over 140 entities, with ownership percentages ranging from 28.5% to 100%, and covers changes during the year such as acquisitions and incorporations.

structure.title: Name of Company

It also describes significant unobservable inputs for Level 3 FVTOCI unquoted equity shares using the DCF method, WACC ranges (12.25%-13.25% in 2025; 11.50%-12% in 2024) and sensitivity impacts, plus a change in valuation technique for Kutch Railway Company Limited.

structure.title: Amortised Cost Instruments and Financial Risk Management Policies
key_items: c) Financial Instrument measured at Amortised Cost
structure.summary: The page covers financial instruments measured at amortised cost, noting carrying amounts approximate fair value since management expects no significant differences from eventual receipts or settlements. It then details financial risk objectives and policies: principal liabilities (loans, borrowings, payables, lease liabilities, guarantees) finance operations and support joint ventures; principal assets include loans, investments, receivables, and cash, plus FVTOCI investments and derivatives. Key risks are market (currency, interest rate, equity price), credit, and liquidity risk, overseen by senior management and managed via derivatives (cross currency, interest rate swaps, forwards, options) under a Board-approved policy by the Central Treasury Team, prohibiting speculative trading. Derivative execution timing varies with market conditions and costs, counterparties are creditworthy, and exposures are monitored. Currency and interest risks are measured daily via mark-to-market from Bloomberg/Reuters and bank quotes, with gains/losses recorded in profit and loss except effective hedge portions.

structure.title: (A) Market risk
structure.summary: The text covers market risk, defined as the risk of fair value fluctuations due to market price changes, comprising interest rate risk, currency risk, and other price risk. It lists affected financial instruments. It describes sensitivity analysis assumptions for March 31, 2025 and 2024, excluding gratuity and post-retirement obligations. Interest rate risk is detailed, including exposure from long-term floating-rate debt, management via fixed/variable mix and swaps/futures, and sensitivity showing a 50 basis point change would decrease/increase profit by ₹32.66 crore (2024: ₹13.28 crore). Foreign currency risk is explained, covering exposure to USD, JPY, AUD, SGD, AED, EUR, CHF, and CNY, management through swaps and hedges, and a 1% sensitivity analysis on net unhedged exposure.

structure.title: Interest Rate Risk and Sensitivity Analysis
structure.summary: This page from the notes to the consolidated financial statements covers interest rate risk and sensitivity analysis. It outlines the basis for sensitivity analysis, including assumptions that net debt, fixed-to-floating ratios, and foreign currency proportions remain constant, excluding gratuity and post-retirement obligations. It details the Group's exposure to market interest rate changes from financing, investing, and cash management, primarily long-term floating-rate debt, and how it manages this through balanced fixed/variable loans and interest rate swaps/futures. The interest rate sensitivity analysis, based on derivatives and non-derivatives at period end, assumes a 50 basis point increase/decrease, showing a ₹32.66 crore decrease/increase in profit for FY2025 (FY2024: ₹13.28 crore), mainly from variable-rate long-term borrowings, calculated on risk exposure at balance sheet date.

structure.title: (ii) Foreign currency risk
structure.summary: The text discusses foreign currency risk, noting that exchange rate movements in USD, JPY, AUD, SGD, AED, EURO, CHF, and CNY against INR impact the Group's operating results. It describes risk management via currency swaps for foreign currency loans, foreign exchange contracts for borrowings and creditors, and cash flow hedges for highly probable forecasted transactions. It states the Group's main exposure currencies and presents a sensitivity analysis table showing the impact of a 1% increase or decrease in each currency rate on pre-tax equity and profit before tax for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, based on net unhedged exposure.

structure.title: Cash Flow Hedge Accounting
structure.summary: This text from Adani Ports and SEZ's 2024-25 consolidated financial statements covers cash flow hedge accounting. It details the Group's risk management policy for hedging foreign currency risk, designating highly probable forecast revenues and non-derivative foreign currency liabilities as hedged items and instruments. It explains recognition of the effective portion in Other Comprehensive Income, prospective discontinuation, immediate recognition of ineffective portions in Profit and Loss, the dollar offset method for effectiveness assessment, sources of ineffectiveness (time value of money and rate differences), key assumptions (6% revenue growth, 4.50%-6.70% discount rates), the 1:1 hedge ratio, and the hedging instrument.

structure.title: Carrying Amount
structure.summary: The text presents financial instrument disclosures from consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It details carrying amounts of foreign currency bonds as liabilities (20,180.65 crore in 2025, 22,986.42 crore in 2024) with maturities from July 2024/2027 to August 2041, classified as non-current borrowings. It covers hedged items: highly probable forecast sales with nominal values matching the bonds, and cash flow hedge reserves in other equity (negative 259.93 crore in 2025, negative 183.95 crore in 2024). It also shows the effect of cash flow hedges in profit and loss, including total hedging loss recognized in OCI (436.15 crore in 2025, 313.68 crore in 2024), income tax effects, amounts recycled to profit and loss, and ineffectiveness recognized.

structure.title: (iii) Equity price risk
structure.summary:
(iii) Equity price risk
The Group’s non-listed equity securities are susceptible to market price risk arising from uncertainties about future values of the investment securities. The Company manages the equity price risk through diversification and by placing limits on individual and total equity instruments. Reports on the equity portfolio are submitted to the Company’s senior management on a regular basis. The Company’s Board of Directors reviews and approves all equity investment decisions.
The Group has given corporate guarantees and pledged part of its investment in equity in order to fulfil the collateral requirements of the subsidiaries and joint venture entities. The counterparties have an obligation to return the guarantees/ securities to the Company. There are no other significant terms and conditions associated with the use of collateral.

structure.title: Credit Risk and Concentrations: Disclosures and Management Policies
key_items: Concentrations of Credit Risk form part of Credit Risk
structure.summary: The page covers credit risk under financial instruments notes. It defines credit risk and identifies exposures from operating activities (trade receivables, other financial assets) and financing activities (loans, bank deposits, forex transactions). It details customer credit risk management: policy, procedures, credit quality assessment, individual credit limits, and impairment analysis (individual for major clients, collective for minor receivables using historical data). It describes treasury management of bank and counterparty credit risk, including approved counterparties, credit limits, annual review, and Finance Committee approval. It discloses corporate guarantees of ₹245.66 crore (previous year ₹339.29 crore) for joint venture credit facilities. It addresses concentrations of credit risk: dependence on large port user customers, 17% revenue (previous 22%) from such customers, long-term cargo contracts, receivables at 39% of total trade receivables (previous 38%), and potential adverse impact from customer loss.

structure.title: (C) Liquidity Risk
structure.summary: The text defines liquidity risk as the risk of difficulty in raising funds to meet financial commitments and the inability to sell assets quickly at fair value. It describes the Company's liquidity risk management framework for short, medium, and long-term funding, noting exposure arises from maturity mismatches. Management strategies include maintaining cash and cash equivalents and adequate bank credit facilities. It presents tables analyzing derivative and non-derivative financial liabilities into maturity groupings (less than 1 year, 1-5 years, over 5 years) based on contractual undiscounted cash flows for March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, covering borrowings, interest payments, trade payables, derivatives, lease liabilities, and other financial liabilities. Notes clarify the table is based on undiscounted contractual maturities, ignores call/refinancing options, variable interest rates may change estimates, and foreign currency liabilities are converted to INR at the reporting date exchange rate.

It includes tabular data on comprehensive income, share in other comprehensive income, and net assets as percentages of consolidated figures. Notes cover a preliminary agreement for an LNG project, the Social Security Code, an arbitration settlement for Adani Murmugao Port Terminal, and impairment testing of goodwill for various cash-generating units.

nodes.title: Notes on LNG Dispute, Social Security Code, and AMPTPL Settlement
nodes.summary: Note 42 details a dispute over an LNG project at Mundra, including a preliminary agreement, capitalized costs, an interim settlement, arbitration claims and counterclaims, with no adjustments made as of March 31, 2025. Note 43 discusses the Code on Social Security, 2020, which has received assent but awaits notification and final rules, so the Group will assess its impact when effective. Note 44 covers AMPTPL's arbitration with Mormugao Port Trust regarding revenue share and capital return, a settlement agreement finalizing royalty at 20% of 1% of ARR, and the reversal of an excess provision of ₹132.35 crore.

nodes.title: 45 Impairment testing of Goodwill
nodes.summary: The text presents Note 45 on goodwill impairment testing for various Cash Generating Units (CGUs) of Adani Ports and SEZ Ltd, showing goodwill carrying amounts as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, totaling ₹7,093.59 crore and ₹6,906.93 crore respectively. It states goodwill was not impaired, with recoverable amounts based on value-in-use calculations using key assumptions like discount rates (7-16% p.a.) and revenue growth rates (5-20%). It also includes Note 46 discussing a dispute with FCI over a field depot lease, revenue recognition stoppage, and the new Indian Railway policy allowing lease migration.

Note 45 covers goodwill impairment testing, listing entities with goodwill, annual testing, and value-in-use assumptions (discount rates 7-16%, growth 5-20%) with no impairment at March 31, 2025. Note 46 details Adani Agri Logistics Limited's lease dispute and resolution at Bandel under the new Railway Policy, including lease extension and resumption of operations. Note 47 describes a concession agreement with FCI, delays, wagon procurement issues, arbitration over operations date and concession period, and ongoing litigation in the Supreme Court.

The text covers three notes to consolidated financial statements. Note 46 describes Adani Agri Logistics Limited's (AALL) land lease extension at Bandel under new Railway Policy, including agreements with Eastern Railway and FCI approval, and settlement of a dispute at Hooghly depot. Note 47 details AALL's concession agreement with FCI, including development of silo terminals, procurement of specialized wagons, disputes over operations date and WPI escalation, arbitration award in AALL's favor, and subsequent appeals pending before Delhi High Court and Supreme Court. Note 48 lists balances with struck-off companies for FY 2025 and 2024, including names, relationships, transaction natures, and outstanding amounts.

This text is from the Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. Note 48 discloses balances with struck-off companies based on available information. It presents two tables: one for balances outstanding as of March 31, 2025, and another for March 31, 2024. Each table lists struck-off company names, relationships (e.g., Customer, Vendor, Share Holder), nature of transactions (e.g., Deposit from Customers, Sundry Debtors, Purchase of materials, Service availed), and outstanding balances in crore, with some figures nullified on conversion. The text also includes page references and section labels.

nodes.title: 49 Details of the funds loaned or invested by the Group to Intermediaries for further Loan or investment to the Ultimate beneficiaries
nodes.summary: The text presents details of funds loaned or invested by the Group to intermediaries for further loan/investment to ultimate beneficiaries for FY2025 and FY2024, including intermediary names, dates, amounts, and ultimate beneficiaries. It includes notes on foreign currency conversion and FEMA/Companies Act compliance, plus complete details of intermediaries and ultimate beneficiaries (names, addresses, relationships). It also covers statutory information (benami property, quarterly returns, crypto, wilful defaulter, layers), standards issued but not effective, an update on a short seller report and SEBI investigations, and exceptional items for FY2025 and FY2024.

nodes.title: Statutory Disclosures, Standards and Regulatory Matters in Consolidated Notes
nodes.summary: This page covers three sections of consolidated financial statement notes: Section 50 lists statutory information confirming no benami property, no required quarterly current asset returns, no crypto trading, no wilful defaulter status, and compliance with layer rules. Section 51 states no new or amended standards have been notified but not adopted. Section 52 discusses prior short-seller allegations, the Supreme Court's direction to SEBI to conclude two investigations, management's belief that these are now concluded, legal reviews finding no irregularities, and three SEBI show cause notices regarding related party transactions, security deposits, fund usage, code of conduct, and shareholding categorization, with management concluding no material consequences.

nodes.title: 53 Exceptional items includes following:-
nodes.summary: The text covers exceptional items for FY2025 and FY2024, including voluntary retirement settlements of ₹104.03 crore and ₹145.43 crore, and a one-time settlement of ₹215.90 crore, plus a reclassification adjustment of ₹157.80 crore. It details a subsidiary's adoption of the new tax regime under Section 115BAA, resulting in expensing MAT credit of ₹455.16 crore as exceptional tax expense. It also describes the divestment of 49% equity stake in Adani Ennore Container Terminal for ₹248.54 crore, recording a gain of ₹603.27 crore. Additionally, it notes US DOJ and SEC actions against an executive director, with no impact on the company's financial statements, and the authorization of consolidated financial statements on May 01, 2025.

nodes.title: Income Tax, Divestment, US Indictment, and Authorization Notes
nodes.summary: The page titled Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, covers four sections. Section 54 explains the adoption of the new tax regime under Section 115BAA by a subsidiary, resulting in an exceptional tax expense of ₹455.16 crore due to MAT credit expiration. Section 55 details the divestment of a 49% equity stake in Adani Ennore Container Terminal Private Limited for ₹248.54 crore, recording a gain of ₹603.27 crore. Section 56 addresses the Company's awareness of a US DOJ indictment and SEC civil complaint against an executive director, noting no impact on the financial statements. Section 57 states the consolidated financial statements were authorized for issue on May 01, 2025.

The text covers four notes to the consolidated financial statements of Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited for the year ended March 31, 2025. Note 54 discusses a subsidiary's election of the new tax regime under Section 115BAA, resulting in an exceptional tax expense from MAT credit. structure.title: GRI Content Index
structure.summary: This GRI Content Index from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 maps disclosures to GRI standards. It covers general disclosures (GRI 2) on organizational details, governance, strategy, and stakeholder engagement; material topics (GRI 3); economic performance (GRI 201), market presence (202), indirect impacts (203), procurement (204), anti-corruption (205), and anti-competitive behavior (206); environmental topics including materials (301), energy (302), water (303), biodiversity (304), emissions (305), waste (306), and supplier environmental assessment (308); and social topics covering employment (401), labor relations (402), occupational health and safety (403), training (404), diversity (405), non-discrimination (406), freedom of association (407), child labor (408), forced labor (409), security practices (410), local communities (413), supplier social assessment (414), public policy (415), customer health and safety (416), and customer privacy (418). Each disclosure references specific report sections and page numbers.

structure.title: UNGC Principles Index
structure.summary: The text presents the UNGC Principles Index, listing Principles 1-2 on human rights, Principles 3-6 on labour (freedom of association, forced labour, child labour, discrimination), Principles 7-9 on environment (precautionary approach, responsibility, friendly technologies), and Principle 10 on anti-corruption. It then provides detailed descriptions for these principles and a section mapping topics like human rights, freedom of association, discrimination, ESG governance, risk, emissions reduction, water stewardship, wastewater, waste, biodiversity, and corporate governance to page numbers in a report.

structure.title: CEO Water Mandate Index
structure.summary: The text presents Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's CEO Water Mandate Index from its Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, outlining pledges across six areas: direct operations (water-use assessment, conservation targets, technology investment, awareness, and decision-making); supply chain and watershed management (supplier encouragement, capacity building, assessments, practice sharing, and reporting); collective action (civil society ties, government collaboration, technology promotion, and UN Global Compact involvement); public policy (regulatory input, advocacy, partnerships, and policy body support); community engagement (understanding local challenges, support, education, and infrastructure development); and transparency (progress reporting, strategy publication, and government transparency). It also includes a chapter index mapping topics like water stewardship, procurement, CSR, ESG framework, and governance to page numbers, plus a final pledge to support water initiatives and collaborate with UN and intergovernmental organizations.

structure.title: Indian Business Biodiversity Initiative (IBBI) Index
structure.summary: The text presents the Indian Business Biodiversity Initiative (IBBI) Index from Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25. It outlines ten indicators: mapping biodiversity interfaces with business operations (15 sites assessed), enhancing employee awareness (35 trained, 58% sensitized, various activities), assessing biodiversity risks and opportunities, considering business decision impacts, setting objectives and targets, designating a biodiversity champion (Mr. Rahul Agarwal), including biodiversity in environmental management systems, encouraging stakeholder support (suppliers, customers, others), engaging in policy advocacy with government, NGOs, and academia (via FICCI, IUCN), and initiating valuation of biodiversity and ecosystem services using the Ecosystem Service Matrix. Each indicator includes chapter names and page numbers.

structure.title: Notice
structure.summary: The notice convenes Adani Ports' 26th AGM on June 24, 2025, via video conferencing. Ordinary business includes adopting audited standalone and consolidated financial statements for FY2024-25, declaring dividends on preference and equity shares, and reappointing Mr. Rajesh S. Adani as a rotating director. Special business includes appointing CS Ashwin Shah as Secretarial Auditor for five years, re-appointing Mr. P.S. Jayakumar as Independent Director for a second three-year term, approving commission to non-executive directors up to 1% of net profits for five years, altering the Articles of Association to delete the common seal clause, and approving material related party transactions with Mediterranean International Ports A.D.G.D Limited, Colombo West International Terminal (Private) Limited, Sunrise Worldwide Enterprise Limited, Ambuja Cements Limited, and ACC Limited for FY 2025-26 and/or FY 2026-27. It also authorizes the Board to appoint Branch Auditors for overseas branch offices.

nodes.title: a) Details of the source of funds in Not Applicable
nodes.summary: The text outlines a proposed related-party transaction between Adani Logistics Limited (ALL), a wholly owned subsidiary, and ACC Limited, a cement manufacturer within the Adani Portfolio. ALL will provide logistics services for inbound/outbound activities and maintenance, with pricing via e-auction and market-based terms, alternatively cost-plus if market price is unavailable. The contract, valued up to ₹1,085 crore for FY2025-26, aims to ensure steady revenue, improve fleet utilization, enhance operational efficiency, and open new markets. It represents 3.50% of the company's consolidated turnover and 51% of ALL's turnover. No loans, advances, or investments are involved, and source of funds is not applicable.

nodes.title: c) Applicable terms, including covenants, Not Applicable

It justifies the RPT as being in the interest of the listed entity and notes that no valuation or external party report is applicable. It mentions that all relevant information is included.
